keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no Greek state shape for 1941-1944 (First Hellenic Republic ends 1940, Kingdom of Greece starts 1945). The pages give no area (page silent), only '7.3 million inhabitants in 1941'; the spec is about 108,200 km2. It holds until the Bulgarian annexation of 14 May 1941; the Dodecanese, which Natural Earth's Greece includes, were Italian ('Italy formally annexed the Dodecanese' at Lausanne) and German-held after the 1943 Dodecanese Campaign, 'formally united with Greece by the 1947 Peace Treaty' (Dodecanese page), so they are subtracted by name (reviewer eu-21-x, 2026-11-01).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe after the Bulgarian annexation of 'eastern Macedonia and most of Western Thrace' (14 May 1941): about 95,300 km2 resolved (without the Dodecanese, subtracted by name). The Evros prefecture of Thrace was German-held but sits inside the East Macedonia and Thrace region that the spec removes, so the shape is a little too small; the Ionian Islands (Italian civil administration) are left out.

ledger.note: 30 April 1941: Georgios Tsolakoglou is appointed prime minister of the occupation government in Athens. 'On 30 April 1941, Tsolakoglou was appointed Prime Minister of a' puppet government (the extract ends there); Axis occupation page: 'began in April 1941 after the German invasion of Greece'; Athens 'fell on 27 April'. Under the armistice terms 'the Germans took the strategically important areas such as the Athens area', 'leaving the rest of Greece to be occupied by the Italians and the Bulgarians'.

region.text: the German zone: Athens (Attica), Thessaloniki and central Macedonia

ledger.note: April 1941: the Germans hold Athens, Thessaloniki and Macedonia. The page has 'the Nazi Germans administering the most important regions of the country, including Athens, Thessaloniki'; Macedonia 'was kept under German control both as a strategic outlet into the Aegean'.

region.text: the Italian zone: 'XXVI Army Corps in Epirus and western Greece'; 'VIII Army Corps in the Peloponnese' (the rest of the Italian zone is not named on the page)

ledger.note: April 1941: the Italians hold most of the Greek mainland south and west. 'XXVI Army Corps in Epirus and western Greece'; 'VIII Army Corps in the Peloponnese'; the page gives the corps, not the day.

region.text: 'eastern Macedonia and most of Western Thrace', handed over to Bulgaria and annexed on 14 May 1941 (read as the East Macedonia and Thrace region)

ledger.note: 14 May 1941: Bulgaria annexes eastern Macedonia and Western Thrace. 'Bulgaria officially annexed the occupied territories on 14 May 1941'; 'eastern Macedonia and most of Western Thrace, were handed over to Bulgaria'; the Bulgarian Army 'entered Greek Thrace' on 20 April.

1 June 1941: Crete falls to Germany. 'by 1 June, after the capture of Crete, all of Greece was under Axis occupation'; Crete went to the Germans 'except for the eastern Lasithi Prefecture, which was handed over to the Italians'.

region.text: the Italian zone: 'XXVI Army Corps in Epirus and western Greece'; 'VIII Army Corps in the Peloponnese' (the rest of the Italian zone is not named on the page)

ledger.note: September 1943: the Italian zone ends. 'After the Italian armistice in September 1943, the Italian zone was taken over by the Germans.'

region.text: the Italian zone: 'XXVI Army Corps in Epirus and western Greece'; 'VIII Army Corps in the Peloponnese' (the rest of the Italian zone is not named on the page)

ledger.note: September 1943: Germany takes over the former Italian zone, Epirus, western Greece and the Peloponnese. 'After the Italian armistice in September 1943, the Italian zone was taken over by the Germans.'

region.text: occupied Greece after the Bulgarian annexation: without the Ionian Islands (Italian civil authorities) and without 'eastern Macedonia and most of Western Thrace', read as the East Macedonia and Thrace region (which also holds the Evros prefecture, German-held)

ledger.note: 12-31 October 1944: the Germans leave mainland Greece. 'German troops evacuated Athens on 12 October 1944, and by the end of the month, they had withdrawn from mainland Greece'; Crete and some islands were surrendered 'by German garrisons in May and June 1945'.

region.text: the German zone: Athens (Attica), Thessaloniki and central Macedonia

ledger.note: 12 October 1944: the German zone of Athens, Thessaloniki and Macedonia is evacuated. 'German troops evacuated Athens on 12 October 1944, and by the end of the month, they had withdrawn from mainland Greece'.

region.text: Crete, where the German garrison held until 1945

ledger.note: October 1944: German rule of the Hellenic State ends, though Crete and some Aegean islands were held until May-June 1945. 'Crete and some other Aegean Islands being surrendered to the Allies by German garrisons in May and June 1945'; the dossier ends in October 1944 with the regime, so the island garrisons are not followed.

ledger.note: 14 October 1944: the Greek government returns to Athens. 'The first British troops under General Scobie arrived in Athens on 14 October 1944.' The land passes from the puppet state to the Kingdom of Greece.

wars.name: Battle of Greece

zones.text: mainland Greece and the Aegean islands that the Tsolakoglou government nominally administered in April 1941, without the Ionian Islands, where 'the Greek civil authorities were replaced by Italians' (Dodecanese not Greek then)

wars.outcome: Germany invaded on 6 April 1941; Athens fell on 27 April; Bulgaria entered Greek Thrace on 20 April and annexed it on 14 May; Crete was taken by 1 June, when 'all of Greece was under Axis occupation'.
wars.note: The Battle of Greece and Battle of Crete articles were not opened (page budget). The Tsolakoglou page dates the surrender protocol to 20 April, its formalisation at Larissa to 21 April and a third ceremony with the Italians to 23 April 1941.

certainty.note: The pages name the zones by region and army corps, not by line; the Bulgarian annexation line, the Italian-German zone line and the Ionian Islands' status are not located.

sources.title: Axis occupation of Greece
sources.note: Invasion 6 April 1941, Athens 27 April, zones, Bulgarian annexation 14 May 1941, Crete by 1 June, Italian armistice September 1943, evacuation of Athens 12 October 1944. The page has no infobox, area or capital.

sources.title: Georgios Tsolakoglou
sources.note: Surrender 20-23 April 1941, appointed prime minister 30 April 1941, head of government to 2 December 1942, armistice terms for the zones.

sources.title: Hellenic State
sources.note: Name page only: the pro-Axis government renamed the country 'Hellenic State' during 1941-1944 while the Kingdom of Greece remained in exile in Egypt.

sources.title: Dodecanese
sources.note: Italian from 1912 ('Italy formally annexed the Dodecanese' under the Treaty of Lausanne), German after the 1943 Dodecanese Campaign, 'formally united with Greece by the 1947 Peace Treaty'; why the Dodecanese are subtracted from the shape (added by the eu-21-x reviewer).

notes: The Wikipedia page 'Hellenic State' covers only the name (First Hellenic Republic 1828-1832, Second Hellenic Republic, the Axis occupation 1941-1944); the regime itself is described in 'Axis occupation of Greece', which has no infobox, so the area, capital and start are from body text and the Tsolakoglou page. Gaps: the Ionian Islands' status under Italy is not located (only 'the Greek civil authorities were replaced by Italians'); the Italian-German zone line, Thessaly and central Greece are not named; the EAM-ELAS 'liberated zones ('Free Greece')' of 1943-1944 (the page says only 'By mid-1943') have no extent or date (no rebel/contest events written); Logothetopoulos's and Rallis's end dates; the Dodecanese (Italian since 1912, German-held from 1943) are outside the shape. The nazi-germany dossier has occupation_start for kingdom-of-greece (German-held part) from April 1941; the eu-22 kingdom-of-greece dossier founds in 1945 without 1941-1944. The Bulgarian annexation is recorded as a loss here; the principality-of-bulgaria dossier (eu-18) should hold the matching gain.
